# Project context (shared by all agents)

## Stack
- Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce, MSI, multi-store / multi-language.
{{FRONTEND_RULES}}
- PHP version: {{PHP}}. NEVER use syntax or functions newer than the project's lowest supported version.
- Magento directory (relative to the project directory): `{{MAGENTO_ROOT}}`. Custom code: `{{MAGENTO_ROOT}}/app/code/<Vendor>/<Module>`. Do not modify `vendor/` or `generated/`.

## Local environment: {{ENV_NAME}}
- Run all PHP/Magento commands inside the container (the container's working directory = the Magento directory):
  - `{{EXEC}} bin/magento <command>`
  - `{{EXEC}} composer <command>`
  - `{{EXEC}} vendor/bin/phpunit ...`
  - `{{EXEC}} vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=Magento2 <path>`
- Database: `{{DB}} -e "<SELECT ...>"` (read only, unless a QA task requires otherwise — see the data rules).
- Store URL: {{BASE_URL}}
- Test e-mails: {{MAIL_URL}}
- Do not stop the environment with volume removal, do not delete the environment and do not import databases without the user's approval.
- Do NOT use `isolation: worktree` or separate worktrees: the environment serves the store from the main checkout, so code in a worktree would be invisible to smoke tests and QA.

## Environments
- We work ONLY on the local environment ({{ENV_NAME}}). Staging only when the user explicitly names it. Production — never.

## Security and data (FWC rules)
- Secrets only through 1Password (`op run`, `op read "op://Vault/Item/field"`). Never output passwords/tokens in files, commands, commits or Jira.
- Client data is confidential. Do not paste raw database rows or logs into Jira, PRs or handoff files — summarize and pseudonymize.
- MCP: agents may use the MCP servers configured for the project (currently: Atlassian — as the project server `atlassian`, the claude.ai connector or the `atlassian` plugin; Playwright is provided by the `magento2` plugin and used by QA in the pipeline). Reads work without prompts; every write to an external system needs the user's approval. New MCP server → first check it is on the "Approved Tools" list; pin the version exactly (no `@latest`).
- Use only tools from the FWC "Approved Tools" list (Confluence). Not on the list → stop and ask.
- Destructive operations (DROP/TRUNCATE, DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE, `rm -rf`, force-push, `reset --hard`, skipping hooks) → require the user's confirmation naming the environment.
- Business rules: Jira/Confluence are the source. Code = current behavior, Confluence/Jira = intended behavior. Divergence → report it, do not resolve it yourself. Never invent rules.

## Handoff files
- Directory: `{{MAGENTO_ROOT}}/var/agents/<KEY>/` (ignored by git). Every `var/agents/...` path in the agent and orchestrator definitions means `{{MAGENTO_ROOT}}/var/agents/...` relative to the project directory.
- The file `var/agents/.current` holds the current issue key (written by the orchestrator; read by the validation hook).
- Files and allowed statuses:
  - `01-analysis.md` — READY | BLOCKED | TOO_LARGE
  - `02-architecture.md` — READY | NEEDS_INPUT | TOO_LARGE
  - `03-test-plan.md` — READY | NEEDS_INPUT
  - `04-implementation.md` — DONE | NEEDS_INPUT
  - `05-review.md` — APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
  - `06-qa.md` — PASS | FAIL
  - `07-retro.md` — (no status)
- Every file starts with the line `STATUS: <value>`, has a `## Success criteria` section (checklist `[x]`/`[ ]`) and `## Open questions` in the format `- → <agent>: <question>` (or "none").
- A positive status with any `[ ]` is rejected automatically by the `SubagentStop` hook.
- QA evidence: QA records Playwright screenshot paths and result summaries in `06-qa.md`.
- After the issue is closed, the `var/agents/<KEY>/` directory is deleted.

## Size, track and brevity
- The business analyst assigns a size to every issue; all agents scale their work and output to it:
  - **S** — bug or small tweak, 1 module, ≤ 3 files, no schema / new configuration / API contract change,
  - **M** — up to 2 modules or ≤ 15 files,
  - **L** — larger (usually TOO_LARGE → split).
- **Fast track** (only "Bug", size S, root cause located in code, fix is obvious, no open questions): the Solution Architect is skipped; the developer works from the "Size and track" section of `01-analysis.md`. The user approves the fast track at the analysis checkpoint.
- Brevity — write only what the next agent needs to act:
  - omit sections that do not apply (always keep `STATUS`, `## Success criteria`, `## Open questions`); do not write "not applicable" paragraphs,
  - success criteria that do not apply: `- [x] n/a — <criterion>`, no explanation,
  - do not restate earlier handoff files — reference them (e.g. "AC1–AC3 as in 01-analysis.md"),
  - bullet points and tables, no prose introductions or summaries of what you are about to do,
  - guideline per handoff file: S ≤ 30 lines, M ≤ 80 lines, L as needed.

## Agent memory
- Solution Architect and Code Reviewer have `local` memory (`.claude/agent-memory-local/`, outside git, per project — so knowledge about one client never reaches another).
- Store only technical knowledge about the project in memory (conventions, pitfalls, recurring remarks). Never client data, personal data or secrets.
